target_customer: Consumers for the lollicam app, then smartphone makers, telcos and app developers for the ARGear AR SDK
problem: Mobile apps and phone makers wanted face tracking AR stickers and effects without building the technology themselves.
business_model: consumer AR camera app with branded stickers, later B2B SDK licensing
product_category: Augmented reality camera app and SDK

founders.name: Michael Chong
founders.background_notes: YC page: over 20 years of technical marketing, product planning and new business development.

founders.name: JaeCheol Kim
founders.background_notes: Called JC in the YC launch post; no bio found.

competitors.name: Snapchat Lenses
competitors.what: Face tracking sponsored lenses inside Snapchat
competitors.traction_then: YC post says sponsored lenses were priced at $450,000 to $750,000 per day

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time face tracking and effects on mobile phones in 2015 was demanding but achievable by a small engineering team.

defensibility.rationale: Branded sticker content and partnerships (Facebook profile videos, Disney Zootopia stickers) helped but platforms such as Snapchat could ship the same effects.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: A Seerslab press release claims Snapchat and Facebook later adopted face tracking stickers; this is self reported. The company pivoted to B2B SDK sales.

market_need_then: The YC launch post (June 2016) cited high growth and retention for lollicam, Facebook and Disney partnerships, and the high price brands paid for Snapchat sponsored lenses.

branding.domain_note: Company site argear.io is the product domain; it did not resolve when fetched in 2026-11.
branding.brand_signature: lollicam, the consumer AR sticker app with branded sticker partnerships
branding.community_and_virality: YC post reports Disney Zootopia branded stickers and a Facebook profile video integration; no fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: The consumer app brand lollicam had partner coverage in 2016, but the company name Seerslab and ARGear had little press about the brand and the ARGEAR US word mark is shown cancelled by one trademark database.

pivots.to: ARGear AR SDK platform for app developers
pivots.why: ARGear was pitched in 2018 as turning a camera feature into a Snapchat style lens within a day; the reason for the shift is not stated.

outcome_analysis: Seerslab began with the lollicam consumer AR app, gained notice at YC in 2016, then moved to selling the ARGear SDK to app developers and phone makers. It kept operating and raising small strategic rounds through 2024 and launched AI glasses in 2025, so the YC Inactive label conflicts with the evidence. The company seems to have survived by pivoting to B2B, though total funding appears modest.
notes: YC lists status Inactive but search shows ongoing operations in Seoul through 2025, so exit type is none. The Series A dates (April and May 2021) rest on CB Insights and The VC, which are databases; no amounts found. The October 2022 Selvas AI strategic equity is reported by Asia Economy; CB Insights labels it Series B-II. The December 2024 KRW 1.55B Bilanx round rests on Preqin alone. Seedtable lists pre-seed 2016-01 and seed 2016-06 pages that returned 403, so those rounds are unverified. Total raised estimates conflict: PitchBook $3.4M, CB Insights $1.42M, Caplight $3.98M. The YC page gives HQ as both Palo Alto and San Francisco while other sources say Seoul. Only one competitor had a dated source.
